chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Aqeeqa, is it obligatory? He said: Yes. An animal is sacrificed for him, and his head is shaved when he is seven days old, and his hair is weighed in silver or gold and given in charity, and the midwife is fed a quarter of a sheep, and the Aqeeqa is a sheep or a camel.

key_terms.ابْنُ سَبْعَةٍ: Seven days old (referring to the timing of the ritual).
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: The sacrifice offered for a newborn child on the seventh day.
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (one of the permissible animals for Aqeeqa).
key_terms.يُوزَنُ شَعْرُهُ: His hair is weighed (to determine the amount of charity).

ai.seo_question: What are the obligations and rituals of Aqeeqa for a newborn in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Yunus ibn Abi al-‘Adi, establishes the Aqeeqa as an obligatory act (wajib) performed on the seventh day, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of naming and shaving. It details the specific rituals, including weighing the newborn's hair to distribute silver or gold in charity and providing a quarter of a sheep to the midwife, thereby linking physical purification with social welfare. The specification of a sheep or camel reflects the standard sacrificial animals in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the communal and familial dimensions of welcoming a new life.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Aqeeqa, is it Obligatory?’

Heasws said: ‘Yes. Perform Aqeeqa for him, and shave off his head when he is a boy of one week, and weight his hair by silver or gold, so give in charity with it, and feed the midwife, a quarter of the ram, and the Aqeeqa is a ram or a camel’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about Aqiqah : if it is obligatory. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, Aqiqah must be offered for him, his head is shaved when he is seven days old and his hairs are weighed with silver or gold to be given in charity. One-fourth of the sheep is served to al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor). The animal for Aqiqah should be a sheep or Badanah (camel of a certain age).”’ ( Al-Qabilah according to hadith number three, chapter ninety-three is a nurse who helps a woman to give birth and also thereafter not the one who helps one to give birth only and then moves away.)
